newsitem.title: GEORGIA: McConnell Dowell wins Georgian pipeline tender.
newsitem.headline: McConnell Dowell wins Georgian pipeline tender.

text.p: McConnell Dowell Middle East, a division of Australia's McConnel Dowell Corp, has won a $60 million tender to carry out work on an oil pipeline through Georgia, John Hollis, senior vice president of the Azerbaijan International Operating Co (AIOC) said on Tuesday.

The AIOC, a 13-member international consortium, has said it intended to use the route, which terminates at the Georgian port of Supsa in the Black Sea, for handling some early oil from its $8-billion project to develop three Azeri Caspian Sea fields.
The consortium is led by British Petroleum Plc and Norway's Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil).

McConnell Dowell, which a Georgian International Oil Corporation (GIOC) press release said specializes in construction works and pipeline projects, will build a 39-km extension of the 530-millimeter diameter pipeline which runs from Georgia's border with Azerbaijan.
GIOC officials said McConnell Dowell would also carry out repairs on other sections of the 380-km Georgian portion of the line, which originates near the Azeri capital of Baku.

Hollis told reporters that a joint venture between the state-owned Azeri oil company SOCAR and private Turkish construction company Tekfen Inshatt ve Tesisat A.S. had won a $60 million tender to carry out repair and construction work on the Azeri portion of the line.
"The work will be completed as fast as possible and we expect the first shipment of oil to arrive in Supsa by the end of 1998," he said.
The AIOC said five companies had competed for the contracts, but it did not name them.
